messages:
sofia: Hey team — customer reported embeddings endpoint returning 'dimension mismatch' after we bumped max_batch_size to 128 yesterday. They also see persistent tail latency spikes (400-800ms) and occasional 400 errors. Repro steps below.

sam: Can you paste the exact error and which model alias they hit? Also SDK version. Could be coalescing or a routing fallback.

sofia: Model alias: open-embed-1024-v2 (hosted). SDK: python-sdk 0.9.3. Error sample: 

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536"}
```

Customer payload is 1536-dim vectors. They say it was fine on max_batch_size=64; we moved them to 128 during a perf test.

kai: Two quick angles: 1) Are requests being routed to a different model variant (1024 vs 1536)? 2) Is dynamic batching merging different-dim requests? The batcher should reject mixed-dim requests, but a bug could allow coalescing then fail later.

megan: I'm seeing a spike on embeddings.batcher.coalesce_window_ms from ~50ms -> 400ms at the incident time. Queue on shard g-03 hit ~120. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/d/embeds/batcher?panel=queue (internal).

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T09:12:01 -> runtime: batcher v2.1.3 rolled to prod on g-03

sam: That v2.1.3 change included the 'snapback' coalescing logic that temporarily raises max_batch_size under load. Possible edge-case: larger max_batch + mixed request sizes leads to long-tail processing. Can you grep the batch logs for "dims" and "pad_len" under /var/log/embeddings/batches/2026-03-15/?

sofia: Minimal repro curl they gave: 

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?model=open-embed-1024-v2 \
  -d '{"input": [[0.0,... (1536 floats) ...]]}'
```

They consistently get the 400 above. But their latency trace shows some requests accepted and processed slowly before failing.

sam: The 400 is usually thrown at validation time. If we're seeing processed-but-failing behaviour, something is buffering or batching mismatched dims and rejection happens later in the pipeline.

kai: Pulled a sample batcher log from g-03: 

```
[2026-03-15T09:14:22Z] Batch[id=8753] dims=[1024,1536,1536] pad_len=[0,512,0] -> queued
[2026-03-15T09:14:22Z] Batch[id=8753] assigned shard=g-03
[2026-03-15T09:14:23Z] Batch[id=8753] start processing -> error: kernel_dim_mismatch
```

If that's accurate, the batcher is mixing dims. pad_len shows we attempted to pad a 1024 entry up to 1536 which is wrong. We should never mix model-dimensioned requests.

megan: Runbook: quarantine shard g-03 and rollback batcher to v2.1.2 (pre-snapback). I'll take roll.

sofia: Customer OK with mitigation. Proceeding to rollback.

deploy-bot: Rollback started 2026-03-15T09:45:00 by megan

megan: Rollback complete. g-03 on batcher v2.1.2. Queue depth normalized within 2m, tail latency trimmed back to baseline. Customer reports success in test requests.

sam: Root cause summary: snapback coalescing in v2.1.3 temporarily allowed increasing the effective max_batch_size and coalescing window which exposed a bug where requests for different model dims could be coalesced. That led to late validation failures and tail latency while the batch attempted GPU processing then errored.

kai: Action items I'll take: open PR to add strict batch-dim validation (fail fast if mixed dims), add unit/integration tests for coalesce window behaviour with mixed-dim traffic, and add metric/alert for batch_dim_mismatch_count.

sam: Also add a canary gate for any future snapback-like changes — don't roll to >1 shard without dim-mix checks.

sofia: Thanks — I'll update the customer and keep the support ticket open until patch is in staging. :thumbsup:
